question: Are the analysers' confidences honest, does the disagreement engine contest what is ambiguous and not what is clear, and which thresholds and weights does the train split ask for - out of sample?

gold.role: check set: nothing tuned on it; every item has one truth

observers.LOCAL_SIGNAL_ANALYZER_V1: production: onset-envelope tempo (60-180), Goertzel spectral key, assumed 4/4 at 0.3, energy-curve sections - all over the rendered mix
observers.TRANSCRIPTION_KEY_V1: production label, oracle input: keyFromNotes over the score's own notes (a transcription at its upper bound, not Basic Pitch output)
observers.NOTE_ONSET_TEMPO_V0: calibration-only: dominant inter-onset interval of the score's notes, folded to 60-180
observers.NOTE_ONSET_METER_V0: calibration-only: bar length from the accent autocorrelation of velocity-weighted onsets on the tatum grid
observers.NOTE_NOVELTY_SECTIONS_V0: calibration-only: cuts where bar-level density / velocity / pitch-class features move
observers.NOTE_CHORDS_V0: calibration-only: estimateChords over the score's notes per true bar (one observer: the chord contest cannot be measured here)

tempo.whatWouldSettleIt: The bar length: a downbeat or metre reading — or the producer tapping the pulse — decides whether the bar holds the faster or the slower count; every beat of the slower reading is also a beat of the faster one.
The metre: a 3:2 tempo ratio is the compound-vs-simple pulse question (dotted quarter in 6/8 against quarter in 3/4); a verified metre settles the tempo with it.

key.whatWouldSettleIt: The tonic: where phrases cadence, the bass at phrase ends, the final chord. Relative keys share every scale note, so pitch content alone cannot tell them apart.
A dedicated key model over the whole recording, or the producer; the readings share no close relation, so at least one is wrong.
The third degree: whether the third above the tonic is major or minor in the melody and the chords.
